title: Terms of Service
intro: These Terms set out the conditions for using MediFinder. Please read them before using the service.
This is a translation of the Korean original. If the two versions differ, the Korean version prevails.

sections.heading: Article 1 (Purpose)
blocks: These Terms define the rights, obligations, and responsibilities between the individual operator of MediFinder (the "Operator") and users of the service (the "Service").

list: 1. "Service" means the medical institution search service provided by the Operator through medifinder.kr and its related applications.
2. "User" means any person who uses the Service under these Terms.

3. "Public data" means information released by public institutions such as the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) and the National Medical Center (NMC), which the Service receives, organizes, and displays.
4. "Medical institution" means the hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies whose information the Service displays. Medical institutions have no partnership with the Operator.

sections.heading: Article 3 (Posting and Amendment of These Terms)
blocks: (1) The Operator posts these Terms within the Service so that users can review them at any time.
(2) The Operator may amend these Terms to the extent permitted by applicable law.

(3) Amendments are announced within the Service at least 7 days before they take effect, stating the changes and the effective date. Amendments unfavourable to users are announced at least 30 days in advance.
(4) A user who does not agree to an amendment may stop using the Service. Continuing to use the Service after the effective date is treated as acceptance of the amended Terms.

sections.heading: Article 4 (Scope of the Service)
blocks: (1) The Service organizes public data so that users can search and view the following information:

list: 1. Basic information about medical institutions — name, address, contact number, institution type, specialties, and opening hours
2. Designation and assessment information released by public institutions, such as specialty hospital designation, number of specialists, and HIRA assessment grades
3. Information released by public institutions or medical institutions, such as costs of non-covered treatments
4. Search by region or location, and display on a map

blocks: (2) The Service does not provide or broker appointments, registration, consultations, telemedicine, or payment. Any treatment relationship is formed directly between the user and the medical institution.
(3) The Service is provided free of charge.
(4) The Operator may change the contents of the Service or add new features.

sections.heading: Article 5 (Source and Accuracy of Information)
blocks: (1) The information shown by the Service is reproduced from data released by public institutions, or processed for display purposes. It is not researched or verified by the Operator.

(2) Public data is reflected according to the update cycle of the issuing institution and may differ from current circumstances. Closures, temporary suspensions, changes to opening hours or specialties, and price changes may not be reflected immediately.

(3) Some names and labels shown in languages other than Korean are machine-translated or assigned by the Operator for display purposes, and may not be the official names used by the institution concerned.
(4) Users must confirm details directly with the medical institution before visiting or receiving treatment.
(5) Errors may be reported using the contact in Article 14 and will be reviewed. Errors in the underlying public data can only be corrected by the issuing institution.

sections.heading: Article 6 (Notice Regarding Medical Care)
blocks: (1) Information provided by the Service is not medical advice or diagnosis, and does not recommend any particular treatment.

(2) The order of search results, the display of assessment grades, and the appearance of a medical institution near the top of a list do not constitute a recommendation by the Operator or any warranty as to the quality of care.
(3) In an emergency, do not use the Service — call 119 or contact the nearest emergency medical institution immediately.

sections.heading: Article 7 (Location Features)
blocks: (1) The Service reads the device's location only when the user actively invokes a location feature, and uses it to search nearby medical institutions and sort by distance.

(2) Users may refuse location use at any time through the settings in the Service or the permission settings of their browser or operating system. The Service remains usable by selecting a region manually.
(3) Details of location data processing are set out in the Privacy Policy.

4. Probe for vulnerabilities or attempt to bypass access controls
